components.gap: The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.absolute-iterated-series is not supplied: the series half of the proof links the corollary's sums to Fubini's integrals only by the bare assertions 'The assumed sum is the first iterated absolute integral, because integration with respect to kappa is summation' (annex 514-515) and 'counting-measure integration of that integrable section equals the sum' (annex 519-521). Neither identity (integral over N+ against counting measure of a nonnegative g equals the sum of g(n); the signed version for an absolutely summable section) is derived in this proof or established anywhere on the route: thm:p15-expectation-law-integral (handbook/parts/p15/integration-expectation.tex 324-348) gives the sum formula only for countable atomic probability spaces. The identification of the hypothesis with Fubini's premise, of H with the section absolute integral (516-518), and of S with Fubini's second section-integral function (522-523) is therefore unwritten. Write the derivation, e.g. the nonnegative series law of thm:p15-nonnegative-integral-laws applied to g = sum of g(n) times the indicator of {n}, each indicator having counting integral one, then the positive and negative parts for the integrable section.

defect_observations.observation: Scored partial: the counting-measure summation identity is asserted three times (premise identification 514-515, H as the section absolute integral 516-518, S as Fubini's section-integral function 519-523) and is not proved anywhere on the route. The closest result, thm:p15-expectation-law-integral, covers only countable atomic probability spaces. The fix is one or two written sentences.

Held PTE5 printed p.41 (PDF p.49), inside the cited extent pp. 37-41 (body line 14), contains Exercise 1.7.3 (Stieltjes integration by parts, three parts) and Exercise 1.7.4 (integral of F(x+c)-F(x) equals c times the total mass). A route-wide search found no treatment of either. Exercise 1.7.5 (printed p.42, outside the cited range) is treated in substance by thm:p15-characteristic-dirichlet-integral (handbook/parts/p15/characteristic-functions-and-inversion.tex:193), which the boundary does not cross-reference. The boundary calls all three 'separate applications' and gives no locator. No component of this unit covers 1.7.3-1.7.4, so this is not scored against C016. Whether they are residual source obligations depends on the author scope records, which this audit was instructed not to open.

Example 2's product measurability cites 'the Borel-product theorem', which thm:p15-product-sections proves for R^r x R^s. The factors here are (0,1) and (1,inf) with trace Borel sigma-algebras, and no trace-of-product identity is proved on the route. A one-step route exists: coordinate projections are measurable by thm:p15-product-sections, and the product and the continuous composition are measurable by thm:p15-measurable-operations. This is a question of whether a written justification is precise (correctness), so it is not scored as a coverage gap. The same remark applies to 'is Borel' in def:p15-triangle-integral (body 250), where the same sentence names the coordinate route.
